title: security-review machine-readable summary (§7)
description: The CI-ingestible block emitted by SKILL.md § 7. A consumer must be able to read this without branching on language or parsing prose. Every field is either enumerated or given a computation rule; the invariants JSON Schema cannot express are listed under x-invariants and enforced generically, against any report, by scripts/report_validator.py's validate_report() — the single function scripts/tests/test_report_schema.py and scripts/tests/test_forward_eval.py's grader both call.
x-invariants: summary.baseline == 'absent' implies changes.regressed == changes.unchanged == changes.resolved == 0 and every finding has status 'new'

len(findings) + counts.overflow == counts.p0 + counts.p1 + counts.p2 + counts.p3 — findings[] is short ONLY by the number declared in overflow. A report claiming 4 findings, overflow 0, and listing 1 is inconsistent, and a consumer cannot tell whether the other 3 were dropped or never existed.

counts.p0 and counts.p1 must equal, exactly, the number of findings[] with that severity — overflow may never apply to P0/P1, since summary.pass is computed directly from these two counts; counts.p2 and counts.p3 must each be >= the number of findings[] with that severity (they may legitimately exceed it, via overflow, but never fall short of what is itemised)

stack containing more than one comma-separated value requires per_stack, keyed by each declared stack name — otherwise a consumer cannot tell which stack a domain failure belongs to; per_stack must not contain an entry for a stack that is not declared in stack

changes.new + changes.regressed + changes.unchanged == len(findings) + counts.overflow — the same reconciliation as the counts invariant, one field over; `resolved` is excluded because a resolved finding is not reported
changes.new, changes.regressed, and changes.unchanged must each be >= the number of findings[] with that status — a declared count may not fall short of what is itemised
every per_stack[*] entry's pass + fail + na must equal security_domains.total — each stack evaluates the same fixed domain set
per_stack[*].failing_domains, when present, must have length == that stack's fail and no duplicates

every per_stack[*] entry in a multi-stack report (stack has more than one comma-separated value) MUST provide failing_domains — this is not optional-but-recommended: a count-only per_stack falls back to a lower bound that cannot tell 'two stacks failing the same domain' from 'two stacks failing different domains', so leaving the field out cannot be allowed to silently downgrade the check
security_domains.fail must equal the size of the UNION of every per_stack[*].failing_domains (not the max, and not the sum — a domain failing in two stacks is one failing domain, not two)
suppressed[*].rule must be one of the numbered rules under SKILL.md's § False-Positive Suppression Rules

pass.description: Gate verdict, computed — not judged. false when counts.p0 > 0 OR counts.p1 > 0 OR security_domains.fail > 0; true otherwise. Both directions are enforced: a clean report may not claim false, and a report with an open P0/P1 or a failing domain may not claim true. An entry in the § 5 Risk Acceptance Register does NOT flip this back to true: acceptance is tracked separately so a CI gate cannot be silenced by a register row.

baseline.description: Whether a prior review artifact was available for the new/regressed/unchanged/resolved diff. 'absent' is the machine form of SKILL.md's 'Baseline not found'.

counts.description: Reported findings per severity. P0/P1 drive summary.pass.

overflow.description: Findings identified but not itemised in findings[] because the report hit its per-severity cap. A non-zero value means findings[] is incomplete and must not be read as the full set. Overflow must never apply to P0 or P1: every P0/P1 finding must be itemised in findings[], because summary.pass is computed directly from counts.p0/counts.p1 — hiding one in overflow would make that computed guarantee fiction. Only counts.p2/counts.p3 may exceed their itemised count.

regressed.description: Existed before and severity or confidence worsened (SKILL.md § Baseline Diff Mode). Not 'previously resolved and back' — that is a `new` finding against the current baseline.

unchanged.description: Present in baseline and still open.

stack.description: Detected stack, or a comma-joined list for a multi-stack repo. Ordering is not significant.

asvs_version.description: One version per report — never mixed. 5.0.0 renumbered 4.x chapters, so a bare requirement ID is ambiguous without this.

active_verification.description: Machine form of the authorization gate's 'Active verification: permitted | NOT permitted' line. 'not_permitted' means every finding was established statically and no reproducer was executed.

security_domains.description: The same key for every stack — a consumer must never branch on language to read this. The retired `go_domains` key must not appear.

required.description: Whether Gate D coverage was mandatory at this review depth.

total.description: The domain set is stack-independent and fixed at 10.

fail.description: Domains with at least one finding. Any value > 0 forces summary.pass false.

na.description: Domains not applicable to this change, each justified in the coverage table. A non-Go stack must not mark all ten N/A.

per_stack.description: Multi-stack repos only: one entry per detected stack, keyed by stack name. A domain is FAIL for the repo if it fails in any stack.

na.description: Domains not applicable in this stack.

failing_domains.description: Which of the 10 domains (by number) failed in this stack. Length must equal `fail`, no duplicates. Not in this object's own `required` array (a single-stack report has no use for it), but scripts/report_validator.py's invariants MANDATE it on every entry whenever `stack` is multi-stack — omitting it does not silently fall back to a merely-weaker check, it is itself a validation error, because a fail-count-only per_stack cannot distinguish two stacks failing the SAME domain from two stacks failing DIFFERENT domains (1 failing domain overall vs. 2).

id.description: Report-local identifier, referenced by the Risk Acceptance Register and the remediation plan.

status.description: Baseline status of a REPORTED finding (SKILL.md § Output Contract: `new/regressed/unchanged`). `resolved` is deliberately absent: a resolved finding is no longer a finding, so it is counted in changes.resolved and does not appear in findings[].

cwe.description: Single primary CWE. Use the most specific one that fits, not a parent category.

asvs.description: Fully qualified: version, chapter, section, requirement. 'Mapping: TBD <reason>' is permitted; a plausible-but-wrong requirement ID is not.

domain.description: Gate D domain this finding belongs to. Omitted — legitimately — when the finding comes from a scenario checklist rather than Gate D: authentication, authorization/IDOR and input validation are Scenario Checklists 1 and 2, not one of the ten domains.

file.description: The anchor a reviewer clicks: 'path:line' preferred; 'path:symbol' accepted where the line number is not stable across the diff.

suppressed.description: Candidates considered and deliberately not reported. Present so a consumer can distinguish 'nothing was looked at' from 'this was examined and ruled out' — the difference an empty findings[] alone cannot convey.

candidate.description: The vulnerability class that was considered, e.g. 'SSRF via http.Get'.

rule.description: Which numbered rule from SKILL.md § False-Positive Suppression Rules justified it. A bare 'looks fine' is not a suppression.

residual_risk.description: The assumption the suppression rests on, and what would invalidate it. Mandated by § False-Positive Suppression Rules ('explain blocking control and residual risk').

allOf.title: pass is computed, not judged: any open P0 forces false
any FAILing security domain forces false
the converse: a clean report may not claim pass false
allOf.description: Without this the rule is one-directional and a report can fail its own gate for no stated reason, which is indistinguishable from a bug in the producer.

allOf.title: ASVS version must not be mixed: 4.0.3 declared
allOf.description: SKILL.md mandates one version per report. A top-level 5.0.0 with 4.0.3 requirement IDs (or vice versa) makes every mapping ambiguous, which is the exact failure the version pinning exists to prevent.

allOf.title: ASVS version must not be mixed: 5.0.0 declared
a baseline diff requires a baseline
